sF_founder_directed_lexical_branch_verdi.evidence: VERDICT ON THE REMAINING LEXICAL FALLBACK: NOT ACCEPTABLE, and stated explicitly rather than implied. Where canonical evidence EXISTS the design is correct and proven (0/13 real names destroyed, 0/18 assertions surviving). Where it is ABSENT the fallback fails in BOTH directions AT THE SAME TIME (10/13 real names destroyed AND 6/18 assertions surviving, 8/18 counting punctuation-only strips). It is not a tuned trade-off point; it has no discriminating power, because it separates 'verbs on a 24-word English list' from 'verbs not on it' and both categories contain both real names and fabricated assertions - 'Terminated Cable Co' survives by the identical accident that lets 'Terminated Bob Smith' survive. REMEDY PROPOSED, honouring the explicit design constraint (no sixth grammar rule): STOP OFFERING THE OPTION. run13/D103 already establishes that an option whose id is absent from the canonical read CANNOT EXECUTE (its id fails the contextCompanyIds provenance filter at index.ts:3047), so it is a dead pointer; offering a selectable choice that can do nothing, labelled with unverifiable model-authored text, is the actual defect and the label gate is downstream of it. Drop options whose id does not resolve against the canonical read before rendering, and ask an open question if that empties the list. This obtains/requires canonical evidence instead of guessing at grammar and collapses both failure directions at once. NOTE THIS RETIRES A COMMITTED CONTRACT: run8/D72b currently pins the opposite, and mutant M20 was killed by run8+run10+lifecycle. It is therefore a founder/product decision, not a patch, and D72b must be retired deliberately rather than broken silently.
